author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: The graph completeness audit scopes every coverage metric to active nodes, so it certifies a saturated graph while 1,796 of 2,079 nodes are unmeasured

pm graph audit is the instrument that decides whether the relationship graph is complete. Every coverage figure it reports is scoped to active items, and 86% of the graph is not active.

Live output on this tracker:

  profile.nodes                      2,079
  profile.edges                      5,071
  profile.active_nodes                 283
  profile.isolated_active_nodes          0
  profile.degree_leq_one_active_nodes    0
  coverage_by_type[T].active / .isolated / .degree_leq_one   -- all active-scoped

There is no terminal, closed, canceled, or all-status counterpart to any of those. The audit therefore reports a fully connected graph — zero isolates, zero degree-one nodes, complete type coverage — on the basis of 283 nodes, while saying nothing about the other 1,796. pm graph analyze, run beside it, reports orphan_count 85 and component_count 102 against the full node set, so the disconnection is visible one subcommand away and invisible to the instrument whose job is to find it.

This is a conformance gap against this item's own parent acceptance criteria, which already require that 'coverage profiles vary by item type, lifecycle state, project profile, age, and role'. Lifecycle state is the one dimension the shipped profile does not vary by; it filters on it instead.

The consequence is that the audit cannot see the deficit the project already knows it has. pm-lnrk records the terminal backfill baseline independently — of 1,793 terminal items, 1,268 have no outbound semantic edge and 1,041 have none in either direction — and none of that is derivable from pm graph audit. The measurement lives in a hand-run analysis and in a memory of a prior session rather than in the instrument, so progress on the largest remaining graph gap has no meter, and any backfill batch has no way to report movement through the governance surface.

Two further observations from the same run, recorded here because they belong to the audit's own reporting rather than to the data. All 11 findings are severity info, including legacy_ordering_cycle with 8 findings across 49 subjects, on a graph that pm graph analyze independently reports as acyclic: false — an ordering cycle is a correctness fact about a dependency graph and info is the severity of a note. And missing_reference_terminal reports 3 subjects against profile.missing_nodes 3, dangling references that survive because the terminal population is out of the audit's coverage scope.

Fix direction: emit coverage by lifecycle bucket rather than filtering to active, keep the active-only figures as a named slice so existing consumers and baselines do not break, and give terminal coverage a severity policy of its own so that a 1,268-item semantic gap is not reported as an absence of findings. Adjacent owners, not duplicates: pm-lnrk owns executing the terminal backfill, pm-bzmeaa owns depth and shortest-typed-path metrics, pm-hnc9w7 owns the legacy edge hygiene batch the audit asks for every run.

Coverage metrics are reported per lifecycle bucket (active, closed, canceled, all) rather than filtered to active, with the active-only figures retained as a named slice so existing baselines remain comparable; The audit reports semantic-edge coverage for terminal items, so the pm-lnrk backfill has a meter inside the governance surface and each batch can demonstrate movement; Cycle findings over order-bearing kinds carry a severity above info, and the audit's acyclicity verdict agrees with pm graph analyze on the same graph; Dangling references are reported regardless of the lifecycle state of the referencing item; A test asserts that adding an isolated terminal item changes at least one reported coverage figure, so the instrument cannot silently stop measuring a population again
The instrument that certifies graph completeness must measure the population where the incompleteness actually is
Turns the largest known graph deficit from an unmeasured hand analysis into a governed metric with a baseline
Terminal lineage backfill becomes reportable and ratchetable instead of invisible to every gate
